notes.notes:
Ladies and gentlemen, welcome……

Simplified and Traditional Chinese version of Sacrifice Your Friends have benn officially released！To celebrate the occasion, there will be a discount of 30% off on Sacrifice Your Friends from June 12 to June 19.

Sacrifice Your Friends supports the features of Shared/Split Screen PvP, Online PvP and Remote Play Together. It presents a fresh take on the H.P. Lovecraft horrific mythos that let you experience its stories with your friends.

notes.title: Welcome to Sacrifice Your Friends
notes.notes:
Welcome ladies and gentleman to [b]Sacrifice Your Friends[/b], the universe's best, first, and thus far only lovecraftian party brawler!

It's a pleasure for us at Astrolabe Interactive to be part of the Steam Summer Festival! Our game's demo features 3 multiplayer arenas and 3 story missions. Try SYF either online or couch, or with a mix of both!

Sacrifice Your Friends is released in [b]Early Access on June 18th[/b], during the Summer Festival. For the first week of Early Access, SYF will be 20% off from the standard Early Access pricing, which is itself 20% off from the full release price!

We have two livestream events during the Summer Festival, so come and meet us!

[b]Thursday, June 18th at 1 pm EST
Friday, June 19th at 1 pm EST[/b]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/032cf351571fcf8edf69cebe7c237d1721605fcd.png[/img]



[b]About Us[/b]


Astrolabe Interactive is an indie game studio based in Montreal, Canada. Astrolabe started 2 years ago with 2 young game designers in a living room. We are now a team of over 15 designers, artists and programmers, and we are proud to release our first large scale video game project. We hope you enjoy our game as much as we enjoyed making it!


[b]Join us on [url=https://discord.gg/Dvxj4pP]Discord[/url]![/b]

notes.title: DevUpdate - March 13
notes.notes:
PAX East is already behind us, and Sacrifice Your Friends is almost ready for release. Meanwhile, I created a little virtual tour of the game’s main hub: the train station.

The station is the headquarters of Miskatonic Travel Co., a mysterious agency dedicated to offering occult tours around the world.

[b]The Tour[/b]

The train station is located in Arkham, Massachusetts. The building’s architecture is heavily influenced by Art Deco. The style’s proeminent uses of luxurious materials, geometric patterns, and classical depictions lends itself well to an impressive look that remains faithful to the game’s 1930s setting.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/d69d904e300f6100e966d10627a9817cf6a20cd0.png[/img]


The travel agency’s booth serves as one of the game’s menu screens. From this location, players can choose whatever they want to play story tours, arena games, tournaments, or simply peruse the game guide.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/58196bcb68478e1a587f3093ebc35f6c09d4ea3c.png[/img]


The back wall of the train station features the ticket booth. This is where players select their characters and choose their next arenas. The booth itself is flanked by two colossal statues of dread lord Cthulhu. For reference, these statues would be about 8 meters (26 feet) tall in real life.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/0e2b784a36197b9636d2f7c755a28534393f1268.png[/img]


Of course, a train station wouldn’t be complete without a train. This majestic machine is the Miskatonic Express, bringing you to your final destination in cozy comfort. The Miskatonic Express is powered by a mighty steam engine sporting a golden depiction of Cthulhu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/fd7867bf25969bbf4fdb91f5b5099b63fa6034c3.png[/img]


Speaking of trains, you may notice the departure board when entering the game. It is usually replaced by the option menu, but it is visible on the bottom left of the start screen. It changes every time you enter the main menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/ff7ede714b61d0bb01bb15c35aff2ee92f67803c.png[/img]


If we take a look upward, you will notice the station has glass ceilings. The glass is adorned with depictions of tentacles, a classic nod to lovecraftian iconography.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/b0f5c5f173b9bc014245dc80f47be8f44a940e16.png[/img]


By the way, you may wonder if there is something behind the camera at the start of the game. Well, yes: there is an actual wall closing the station. There is no exit, however. (Except the actual quit button… or Alt+F4 for the villainous barbarians.)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/8f1ad6b68dba70444347b11354336816f778f4a4.png[/img]


[b]Behind the scene[/b]

This was the tour of the train station, SYF’s main hub. I included below a couple behind the scene screenshots.

One of the things I personally do in Sacrifice Your Friends is lighting and postprocessing. To get an idea of what this is about, here is a shot of the station with what I usually call “Wal-Mart lighting”, which is typically what a scene looks like before I work on it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/3e2ba85462dd2d543a5ba865d9c3f4e1e78e9b5a.png[/img]


Here, we have a shot of the station from outside the visible area. To scale, the entire surface is about 45m x 30m (150 ft x 100 ft). The ceiling is 12m (40 ft) high.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/001506d7d61cf6a7369fc9a502b70154807d70c9.png[/img]



Don’t forget to add the game on your [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1050160/Sacrifice_Your_Friends/]Steam wishlist[/url], and follow us on [url=https://www.facebook.com/SacrificeYourFriends/]Facebook[/url]!

Comments or questions? Join us on Sacrifice Your Friends’ public Discord server!

I had a lot of fun writing this update. Next one is likely to be about one of the playable arenas. Hit me up on Discord if you have a specific topic you would like me to cover. Until next time!

By Non-Euclidian Overlord
[i]Game Designer, Astrolabe Interactive[/i]

notes.title: DevUpdate - February 14
notes.notes:
In the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/gid/103582791465114302/announcements/detail/1716370267876413382]previous update[/url], we talked about the context of SYF’s story tours. Now let’s have a look at why we are making a story mode for Sacrifice Your Friends.

[i]All gameplay screenshots displayed in this update are from an early test version of the story mode. Everything you see here is likely to change before release.[/i]

[b]Learning[/b]

The story tours of SYF are good at introducing the lovecraftian universe at the core of the game. However, it is also meant to reveal the gameplay secrets that make SYF such a fun game to play.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/4fad217c2b88427a555574a3111cbb880b53f226.jpg[/img]

While we designed Sacrifice Your Friends’ controls to be simple and intuitive, there is still much newcomers have to learn. Noticeably, we have noticed players often struggle with key elements of gameplay, such as madness, transformation, item charging, and item throwing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/2dea3ab294e0847e08756678ba585632fe74e9bb.jpg[/img]

The story mode is the perfect opportunity to familiarize players with more arduous mechanics. This is not to say the entire campaign is one giant tutorial. Rather, we aim to provide enjoyable solo / coop gameplay challenges centered around a variety of already existing mechanics.

[b]Unlockables[/b]

Mastery is good and all… but what about rewards? At the end of each mission, a rank is awarded to players based on their performance:

[list]
[*] Bronze, which is fairly easy but is needed to move on to the next mission.
[*] Silver, which generally requires a bit of smart play to achieve.
[*] Gold, which often requires a well coordinated team and a good amount of skills.
[/list]

There is even rumors of a mysterious fourth rank that can only be achieved through a truly hardcore level of efficiency.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/70ad13561deb159130041df5b9bdf343513c875f.jpg[/img]

Players earn unlockable elements upon receiving mission ranks. Note that we do not wish to lock gameplay related elements behind overly long or difficult challenges. As such, arenas, items, and cults can all be received by completing bronze level requirements. Players can discover all arenas and acquire basic skills before quickly jumping into competitive multiplayer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/8a059ff6736834b71feba4a27fa628218d53df37.jpg[/img]

For those pushing to the next steps, there are also plenty of customisation items to be earned by achieving silver and gold ranks. These include exclusive characters and accessories to show off your completionism. Unlike experience rewards from playing arena mode, story rewards are shared across all profiles.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/41b11a9f672e08bd84f0ceda9afe512b08d68560.jpg[/img]

In the end, SYF remains a competitive brawler at heart. While we don’t plan on creating a massive storyline for the game, we do plan on it being fun. The story tours should bring interesting context and challenges to the mix.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/fb2eb22034e21fdcea07f99d25f272241f073f51.jpg[/img]

Don’t forget to add the game on your [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1050160/Sacrifice_Your_Friends/]Steam wishlist[/url], and follow us on [url=https://www.facebook.com/SacrificeYourFriends/]Facebook[/url]!

Comments or questions? Join us on Sacrifice Your Friends’ public Discord server!

Next update, I will discuss the game's main hub: the train station. There are a lot of cool little details going into it, so stay tuned!

By Non-Euclidian Overlord
[i]Game Designer, Astrolabe Interactive[/i]

notes.title: DevUpdate - January 31
notes.notes:
Sacrifice Your Friends has entered its last phase of development. Since the end of Closed Beta, we have been extremely busy with the last big feature of the game: Story Mode. Now that the story of SYF is starting to take shape, it seems like a good time to discuss what it entails.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/16cae53f5683b6acf9801a332b790dc13a3c1b3f.jpg[/img]

[h2]The Context[/h2]
Sacrifice Your Friends is set in the universe of author H. P. Lovecraft (1890-1937). While Lovecraft’s work is highly significant in terms of supernatural horror, it's also an important part of modern pop culture.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/ea9401926eb7714668045fced8929815ba207a1a.jpg[/img]

Obviously, SYF has a much lighter tone than Lovecraft’s original work: we are aiming for ironic comedy, not horror. However, we do strive to be faithful to Lovecraft’s mythos.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/5a7bfcb5b8a8af0a64794e75f974f676dd544864.png[/img]

One way this is achieved is by not directly following the plotline of existing stories. Instead, players are invited to explore the world of Lovecraft with the Miskatonic Travel Co., a shady travel agency. The agency offers a positive outlook on ritual sacrifices and malevolent cosmic entities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/d69d904e300f6100e966d10627a9817cf6a20cd0.png[/img]

The train station, which players will recognize as the game’s hub area, serves as the MTC’s headquarters. From this location, players can plan their occult world tours in all the cozy opulence they may desire.


[h2]The Shape[/h2]
The Miskatonic Travel Co. will offer four to five guided tours, each going through four arenas. Each mission has custom objectives and narration. Players earns rank depending on the team’s overall performance. All missions are cooperative, and can be played solo. Mission difficulties and rank requirements change with the number of players in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/d41a59d98606092fce33b2813616a87bce2d482f.png[/img]

The tours are narrated by the Guide, a fully voiced character that will accompany the players as they progress through their occult getaway. We are currently finalizing talks with a professional voice actress for the role. An official announcement should come shortly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/a32e6f737f8f296e74c81385499baaaba71a2f49.png[/img]

Don’t forget to add the game on your [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1050160/Sacrifice_Your_Friends/]Steam wishlist[/url], and follow us on [url=https://www.facebook.com/SacrificeYourFriends/]Facebook[/url]!

This update is the first of two regarding the story of SYF. Next week, we will talk about the purpose of the story in the game. Until then, see ya!

By Non-Euclidian Overlord
[i]Game Designer, Astrolabe Interactive[/i]

notes.title: Closed Alpha - Update v0.8
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/16cae53f5683b6acf9801a332b790dc13a3c1b3f.jpg[/img]

Today, we are releasing version 0.8 of our SYF’s closed alpha! This major update brings numerous exciting new features including the highly requested Online Play! Invite friends via Steam or manually send room codes and join up for a game through the endless nether realms of the internets.

Participants wishing for additional Steam keys to give to their friends can send me a message via private message on Discord. We will be hosting online games with Alpha tester during the next month, so fellow to the SYF Discord channel and join up! Streamers, we can join up with you and play a few matches live if you invite us in advance.

Version 0.8 is not just about online play however: players will be able to try out the new Cult features. Cults are a complete rework of the old “Madness” mechanic. When your stress bar is full, unleash the power of your cult and transform into an avatar of your chosen Ancient. Only the cult of Cthulhu is ready for testing at the moment, but more are coming in the next few months. Yes, you read that right: you can be Cthulhu.

Here is the brief version of patch note 0.8.2.1:
[list]
[*] Updated our engine from Unity3D 2018.3 (HDRP) to Unity3D 2019.2 (HDRP).
[*] Added online play.
[*] Added the Cult of Cthulhu.
[*] Added progression system.
[*] Added unlockable hats.
[*] Added player intro before games.
[*] ... and much more!
[/list]

The full patch note can be found here: https://steamcommunity.com/games/1050160/announcements/detail/2978491455739769620

See you all in the arena!

notes.title: SYF alpha version 0.8.2.1
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35592894/16cae53f5683b6acf9801a332b790dc13a3c1b3f.jpg[/img]

[b][u]Engine[/u][/b]
We are updating our game engine… this might seem a rather boring change to start off with, but trust us: it’s important.
[list]
[*] Updated from Unity3D 2018.3 (HDRP) to Unity3D 2019.2 (HDRP)
[*] Post-processing effects have been completely redone with the new API.
[*] Removed the option to change Bloom settings.
[*] Added the option to change Fog settings. Changing the Fog from Volumetric to Simple can bring major performance gains on lower-end hardware.
[/list]
[i][b]Dev Note 1:[/b] This update brings numerous stability improvements and numerous new features for us to use.[/i]

[i][b]Dev Note 2:[/b] Keeping up with the new release of Unity will pave the way to console porting. From the start, we have been using very powerful experimental features of Unity such as the High Definition Render Pipeline and the VFX Graph. These features were a bit too volatile for console until recently, but after discussion with devs at Unity we are now assured that porting will be able to begin before the end of 2019 on XBox and PS4, and in Spring 2020 for Switch.[/i]


[b][u]New feature : Online Play[/u][/b]
It’s finally here! Thanks to everyone for their patience. We hope you have fun! Alpha testers wishing for additional Steam keys to give to their friends can send a private message to Non-Euclidean Overlord on Discord.
[list]
[*] Added the ability to play online with friends.
[*] Players can host games and invite other competitors via their Steam friends list or by sending a room code.
[*] For online play, multiple players can play from the same computer with other players on another computer. (Ex.: You can play a 4 players game with 1 player on computer A (the host), 2 players on computer B and 1 player computer C.)
[*] Temporarily disabled the Crypt of Alhazred as it is not yet ready for online play. It will be returning in the coming couple of weeks.
[/list]
[i][b]Dev Note:[/b] Let’s be honest, this is the first alpha release of the online multiplayer. There will be bugs, there will be desynchronizations, there will be crashes. It’s just not very stable at the moment. Please report any issues on the #bug-report channel of the SYF Discord. We will keep the alpha updated as issued are found and fixed.[/i]


[b][u]New feature : Cults[/u][/b]
We are completely revamping the “Madness” mechanics. Now, players can choose a Cult; once the Stress bar is full, triggering the Madness will transform the player into a monstrous avatar of their chosen Great Old One! While transformed, players have access to mighty attacks and new abilities. The Stress bar gradually drains for the duration of the transformation, but the opponents can speed up the process by inflicting damage.
Added the Cult of Cthulhu, the first to be added to the game.
The Avatar of Cthulhu offers a mighty close-quarter moveset with the following abilities:
[list]
[*] [b] [Attack Button] [/b]Ancient Claws: The Avatar performs a quick and brutal strike, similar to unarmed combat, only far more powerful.
[*] [b][Dash Button][/b] Greater Dash: The Avatar performs a Dash that covers greater distance than the regular Dash. Very useful to close up on helpless victims!
[*] [b][Grab Button][/b] Coming soon! (For now, this does the same base attack as the Attack Button)
[*] [b][Madness Button][/b] To the Stars:While on the ground, the Avatar leaps into the air.
[*] [b][Madness Button][/b] To the Depths: While in the air, the Avatar slams the ground with great force. Just be careful not to actually slam into the void.
[*] [b][Passive][/b] Winged Aspect: While in the air, the Avatar glides to slow its descent.
[/list]


[b][u]New feature : Progression system[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Experience is now awarded based on game performance.
[*] Profiles can level up, unlocking new characters, skins... and hats.
[*] Added hats to the character selection menu.
[/list]
[i][b]Dev Note:[/b] The progression system is still early in development. It will be progressively expended in the coming months. [/i]


[b][u]Match intro[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Replaced the old countdown sequence at the beginning of each match by a quick close up of every player.
[*] Added an option to disable the player intro.
[*] The loading screen before a match now features a preview of the players and the arena being played.
[/list]
[i][b]Dev Note:[/b] We will most likely modify which information are displayed on the loading screen in the coming weeks.[/i]


[b][u]Others[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] General post-processing now change as the game progress, getting progressively stranger and darker.
[*] Added an option to disable controller vibration.
[*] Added an option to disable screen shake.
[*] Reduced shadow resolution of certain light emitters.
[*] Replaced the model of the bridge in Manuxet Bridge. The new bridge is wider than the old one. The textures of the bridge will be modified in the following week to better harmonize with the surrounding structures.
[*] Removed the old music from the game. Expect the new soundtrack in the next couple months.
[*] Fixed some issues with end game animation.
[*] And lots of minor fixes and improvements...
[/list]
